subject: Fielded product rights, output title and feedback-license — next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Price <samantha.price@heliosanalytics.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Helios Contracts <contracts@heliosanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form (fielded product rights) — questions

Marcus / Ben,

Thanks for the draft order form. We're excited to move forward but the legal team flagged a few items related to the "fielded product" use case we wanted to clarify before we proceed. High-level asks: 

- Output ownership: our product team needs clarity on whether outputs produced by the service (and then embedded into our customer-facing workflows) are assignable or whether Redwood reserves rights for training/model improvements.
- Training & feedback license: the order form currently references a general feedback license. Can you confirm if there's an explicit opt-out for sensitive data or a toggle at the order-form level (we can't accept indiscriminate retraining on PII-derived prompts)?
- Productization fee / carveout: if Helios wants an affirmative downstream productization right (resell/redistribute outputs to our customers), is that a commercial add-on or available by default?

Attaching the order form excerpt we redlined (Draft_OrderForm_v3.pdf). We'd like to resolve language this week and get a final sign-off. Is someone at Redwood available for a 30 min sync tomorrow?

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Price
Head of Legal Ops 
Helios Analytics

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@heliosanalytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form (fielded product rights) — questions

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Quick read-through below and a proposed path forward.

1) Output ownership
- Proposal: Helios retains title to Customer Content and any Outputs that are direct transforms of that Content for use within Helios applications (non-exclusive license to Helios). Redwood reserves the right to use aggregated, de-identified outputs to improve service quality unless Helios expressly opts out via the Order Form (checkbox option: "No training / no feedback license").
- Draft clause language idea: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Content and any Outputs generated solely from such Customer Content. Redwood may use anonymized and aggregated de-identified outputs for product improvement unless Customer selects the 'No Training' option in Section X of this Order Form."

2) Training & feedback license
- We can add an explicit opt-out toggle on the Order Form. Operationally, opting out will trigger a runtime flag and an entry in the per-customer training-lockbox so we can enforce no-retain on KV cache and no-inclusion for offline retraining. There is a small throughput/cost delta when opt-out is active; we will document it in the SOW.

3) Productization fee / carveout
- If Helios requires an affirmative downstream commercialization right (redistribute the model outputs as a product feature to Helios' customers), propose this as a paid addendum (one-time productization fee + higher usage tiers). Without the addendum, Helios gets a broad non-exclusive output license for in-app use but not for creating a derivative model or reselling outputs as a standalone product.

Next steps: I'll draft tracked-change language and send a redline. Can we lock a 30-min call tomorrow at 10:30 PT to walk legal & product teams through the operational controls? I copied Ben for procurement details.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer & Legal Strategy 
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RL_redlines_marcus_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 96 KB)
